name: date-field
title: Date field
purpose: A native date input, or date and time input, as the control of a field, with a hint for what to enter and its earliest and latest values.
whenToUse: For one calendar day the reader knows or picks: an expiry date, the start of a filter.
With type="datetime-local", for a day and a time together, such as when a scheduled run starts.
whenNotToUse: For a date the reader knows by heart and that is far in the past, such as a date of birth. Use three fields: day, month and year.
For a rough span of time, such as the last 7 days. Use a select or a segmented control of ready-made ranges.
For a length of time, such as 30 minutes. Use a number field with a unit.
To show a date the reader cannot change and will not send with a form. Write it as plain text, such as 14 March 2026.

variants.name: date and time
variants.use: input type="datetime-local". At most 286px wide. Set step, in seconds, to limit the minutes it offers.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall. The calendar button inside it is the browser's own, with a widened pointer target.

accessibility: Use input type="date" or type="datetime-local" carrying gw-field__control and gw-date-field, inside gw-field. The label, description and error are the field's. There is no wrapper and no custom calendar.
The value, min and max are always written as 2026-11-22, or 2026-11-22T09:30 with a time, whatever the reader sees. The browser shows and reads the date in the reader's own format.

Because that format and the order of its parts differ from reader to reader, the hint never spells a pattern such as DD/MM/YYYY. The description gives the earliest and latest day with the month as a word, such as Any day from 24 August to 22 November 2026, which also shows the reader what a full date holds. For a time, it names the time zone.
Set min and max to the same range the description gives, and check the value on the server as well: a browser may let the reader type a day outside the range.
For a day out of range, set aria-invalid="true" on the input and link a gw-field__error that names the limit and says what to choose.
The keyboard is the browser's own: Tab moves between the day, month and year, the arrow keys change each, typing digits fills it, and in most browsers Space, or Alt and Down, opens the calendar.
An empty input shows the browser's own outline of the format. Do not add a placeholder.
A read-only date stays focusable and can be read. A disabled one leaves the tab order, and its description says how to make it available.
